key_insight: DOPD improves on-policy distillation by dynamically choosing whether token-level supervision should come from a privileged teacher or privileged student, reducing privilege illusion and preserving transferable capability signals.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a more stable and effective distillation strategy for deploying smaller LLMs and VLMs, especially when high-quality supervision is sparse or uneven across tokens.
method: Routes each token’s supervision based on advantage gap and relative probabilities.
Uses dual distillation from both privileged teacher and privileged student policies.
Applies different supervision strength, objective, and strategy to different tokens to avoid conflating capability gaps with information asymmetry.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive experiments on both LLM and VLM settings, plus stability, robustness, continual learning, and out-of-distribution evaluations, where DOPD consistently outperforms Vanilla OPD and other baselines.
watch_item: The routing logic adds implementation complexity and may depend on careful calibration of token-level advantage and probability estimates to avoid unstable supervision decisions.
